solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greek character taking no notice of a fish shop

indicators.note: ignoring the word a means that letter is dropped from the Greek character

parts.note: beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet
a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish

explanation.surface: A Greek man walks past a fishmonger's without paying it any attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Accept members carry weapons

parts.note: to bear something is to put up with or accept it
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: A club agrees that its members may go armed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being armed, as in the American constitutional right, is a direct synonym for carrying weapons.

clue.text: Tower in area of land ahead of soldiers

indicators.note: the area of land is placed in front of the soldiers in the answer

parts.note: a tract is an expanse of land
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: A tower stands in some territory in front of the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' looks like a building, but read it as one who tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm vehicle that pulls ploughs and trailers is literally something that tows.

clue.text: Group of stars with capital American lawyer

parts.note: and can mean with, along with
Rome is the Italian capital
a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A constellation is linked to a US attorney in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern constellation, named after the princess of Greek myth, is a named group of stars.

clue.text: Block in old boy's vehicle briefly, at end of street

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil; the 's is kept as S

indicators.note: briefly says the vehicle word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a truck is a goods vehicle

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word street

explanation.surface: An old boy's lorry, parked at the end of a road, is causing a blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: To block a passage or a plan is to impede it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Invalid desiring bottom flat?

indicators.note: invalid read as not valid tells us the letters are to be reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sick person longs for a ground-floor apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a noun for a sick person but is the anagram signal, stressed on its second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room combined bedroom and living room is a small rented flat, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Article about one female pickpocket

indicators.note: about says the article goes around the other letters

parts.note: the is the definite article
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A newspaper article tells of a woman who picks pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket is one particular kind of person who steals, so this is an example.

clue.text: Excavate part of chateau near Thionville

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Digging is going on at a French castle close to Thionville in Lorraine.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something up out of the ground is to excavate it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: After end of diet, say yes to fat

indicators.note: after places the agreeing word behind the single letter
end of takes the closing letter of the word diet

parts.note: to allow is to say yes to, to permit

explanation.surface: Having finished the diet, someone gives in and accepts fatty food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered animal fat used for candles and soap is a specific kind of fat.

clue.text: In hope rather than expectation, cricket sides seize the opportunity

indicators.note: seize says the two sides grip the word the between them

parts.note: on and off are the two halves of a cricket field, either side of the batter
taken as written
a chance is an opportunity

explanation.surface: A cricket team grabs its chance, hoping more than expecting.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (or leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing something just in case, with hope rather than expectation of success.

clue.text: Left group, one featured in commercial

indicators.note: featured in says the group and one sit inside the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a band is a group of musicians
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pop group quits after one of its songs appears in an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Left in the sense of deserted or forsaken, a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: I deliver cards for model

parts.note: to deal is to hand out playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being the perfect card dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example to copy is a model, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Popped into a church in ancient city

indicators.note: popped suggests bursting apart, so the word into is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone nipped into a church in an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popped into' reads as dropping into a church, but 'Popped' is the anagram signal working on 'into' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A city of the ancient world in Syria, now Antakya in Turkey, is an ancient city.

clue.text: Severe fire in plant close to Cairo

parts.note: a fern is a plant

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word Cairo

explanation.surface: A blaze breaks out in a factory near Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory; it is a fern.
explanation.definitionFit: A raging blaze is called this, borrowed from the Italian for hell.

clue.text: Inspector again arresting leader of sect

indicators.note: arresting says the word for again holds the next letter

parts.note: more can mean again, as in once more

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of sect

explanation.surface: A detective once again arrests the head of a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional Oxford detective holds the police rank of inspector.

clue.text: Dismissed Tory there and then

parts.note: a batter who is dismissed in cricket is out
Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: A Conservative is sacked on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at once and completely, as in killed instantly, matches the phrase for on the spot.

clue.text: Unconventional Irish soldier?

parts.note: a regular is a professional full-time soldier

explanation.surface: A Republican guerrilla is not a standard soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the noun sense, a guerrilla fighter outside a regular army.
explanation.definitionFit: Not following the usual rules or pattern is a straightforward adjective synonym.

clue.text: Allowed to enter course for a game

indicators.note: to enter says the allowed word goes inside the course

parts.note: a route is a course to follow
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Admitted to a racecourse in order to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino game with a spinning wheel and ball is an example of a game.

clue.text: Fiery liquid makes soldier very loud at home

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud
in means at home

explanation.surface: A loud soldier at home behaves like a hothead.
explanation.definitionFit: A flammable fuel oil for lamps and heaters is a liquid that burns.

clue.text: A leader of monks, I deduced

parts.note: a prior heads a priory of monks

explanation.surface: A monastery's head declares his conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for from what comes before: reasoning from principles, deduced rather than observed.

clue.text: Cycled round in riding competition

parts.note: rode as in rode a bicycle
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A cyclist went round during a show-jumping event.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest of bronco and bull riding is a competition in riding.

clue.text: Shortage of water could be difficult in outskirts of desert

indicators.note: in says the difficult word sits inside those outer letters
outskirts means the outer letters of the word desert

parts.note: rough can mean difficult, as in a rough time

explanation.surface: A water shortage is hard on the fringes of the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A long period without rain is literally a shortage of water.

clue.text: Shun European champ collecting prime piece of silverware

indicators.note: collecting says the other letters gather up the piece of silverware

parts.note: to champ is to chew noisily

indicators.note: prime piece of takes the first letter of silverware

explanation.surface: A European champion steers clear of collecting a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like a winner; it is the verb to munch.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid deliberately is to shun, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Withdraw cash

definitions.meaning: to pull out of a race, as a horse is withdrawn

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: pulling a runner from a race, and slang for ready money.

clue.text: Examine stone in date

parts.note: to try a case in court is to examine it
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A geologist checks a stone on a set day.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovers' secret appointment is a romantic date.

clue.text: Toy dog barking during short march

indicators.note: during says the reworked letters come in the middle
short says the last letter of the march word is cut off

parts.note: a rally is a protest march

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of dog are scrambled

explanation.surface: A toy dog yaps on a brief protest walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for mad, used here as the anagram signal; 'short' trims the protest-march word.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy cloth doll is a child's toy, and also a breed of cat.

clue.text: Old English in one of the Orkney Islands? Nonsense!

indicators.note: in says the old language sits inside the island name

parts.note: Hoy is an island in the Orkneys, off northern Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at Old English being spoken on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for nonsense, an exclamatory synonym like balderdash.

clue.text: What may shine in darkness around Noel, possibly?

indicators.note: around says night goes around the scrambled name

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

indicators.note: possibly says the name Noel may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A festive glow may brighten the dark around Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noel' suggests Christmas lights, but it is anagram fodder signalled by 'possibly', with 'around' as the container signal. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing gas-filled tube sign is something that shines at night.

clue.text: Quaker poet, more humorous about husband

indicators.note: about says the funnier word goes around the husband letter

parts.note: wittier means funnier

explanation.surface: A Quaker poet is funnier than her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: John Greenleaf Whittier was a nineteenth-century American Quaker poet and abolitionist.

clue.text: Summons ambassador — that'll make one squirm

parts.note: a writ is a legal summons
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Serving a summons on an envoy is bound to make someone uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist and wriggle in pain or embarrassment is to squirm, a verb synonym.
